title: Quick check: Understanding Reconciliation

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Understanding Reconciliation”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Comparing element types and keys should preserve stable identity and render the UI derived from the current data.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Comparing element types and keys should preserve stable identity and render the UI derived from the current data.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Understanding Reconciliation: Comparing element types and keys should preserve stable identity and render the UI derived from the current data.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Comparing element types and keys?
options: Use stable identifiers as keys and derive visible lists from current data.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Use stable identifiers as keys and derive visible lists from current data.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Understanding Reconciliation: Use stable identifiers as keys and derive visible lists from current data.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Understanding Reconciliation” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Understanding Reconciliation: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
